# RATIÉ CH. — INTRODUCTION (recognition & the problem of identity)
*Per-chapter analysis for the thesis: recognition as the felt re-cognition of the self.
Companion to `RATIE-EXCAVATION-EN.md` (the full excavation) — this is the IPK-linked,
thesis-targeted literature review of each chapter. Source lines 1104–2548.*

---

## 1. THE CHAPTER'S THESIS (in one line)
Self-recognition is a felt surprise that reveals both my identity and my alienation — and
the Pratyabhijñā is the response to the Buddhist claim that all recognition is illusory.

## 2. EXTENDED QUOTES (French verbatim + English translation)

### Q1 — The paradox of self-recognition (lines 1110–1133)
> "Rien n'est plus familier ni plus mystérieux peut-être que le phénomène de la
> reconnaissance de soi. Familier, il l'est car nous en faisons l'expérience quotidiennement
> : nous reconnaissons notre visage sur telle photographie de famille jaunie… Cette
> reconnaissance peut s'accompagner d'une certaine satisfaction (« je n'ai pas tant changé
> que ça ») ou d'un soupçon d'effroi… Elle prend toujours, fût-ce fugitivement, la forme
> d'une surprise, car nous réalisons alors brusquement ce que nous savions jusque-là sans
> le savoir : que ça, c'est moi."
> **"Nothing is more familiar, or perhaps more mysterious, than the phenomenon of
> self-recognition… This recognition can be accompanied by a certain satisfaction ('I
> haven't changed that much') or a hint of dread… It always takes, even fleetingly, the
> form of a surprise, for we then suddenly realize what we knew until then without knowing
> it: that *that*, is me."**

**→ THE THESIS NODE.** The *satisfaction* and *surprise* of recognition are the felt
register (camatkāra). This is the phenomenon the paper claims is the felt re-cognition of
the self.

### Q2 — Recognition is victory and defeat (lines 1120–1133)
> "Il y a quelque chose de victorieux dans cette banale réalisation : la confirmation que…
> je demeure le même – que je possède une identité. Mais l'événement de la reconnaissance
> est aussi l'aveu d'une terrible défaite : si je dois me re-connaître… c'est bien que je ne
> suis pas tout à fait celui que j'étais… que je suis le même et cependant autre."
> **"There is something victorious in this banal realization: the confirmation that… I
> remain the same — that I possess an identity. But the event of recognition is also the
> confession of a terrible defeat: if I must re-cognize myself… it is that I am not quite
> the one I was… that I am the same and yet other."**

**→** Recognition = "le même et cependant autre" ("the same and yet other"). The
re-cognition presupposes a difference from self (alteration without alterity).

### Q3 — The soteriological stake (lines 1232–1242)
> "Je sais que je suis moi-même – faute de quoi je ne me reconnaîtrais pas ; mais je ne sais
> pas qui je suis – faute de quoi je n'aurais pas à me reconnaître… c'est dans la mesure où
> je demeure étranger à moi-même que je suis privé d'une liberté."
> **"I know that I am myself — otherwise I would not recognize myself; but I do not know who
> I am — otherwise I would not have to recognize myself… it is insofar as I remain foreign
> to myself that I am deprived of a freedom."**

**→** Alienation = misrecognition. Suffering is not-knowing-who-I-am.

## 3. IPK LINKS
- **ĪPK 1.1.1** (the maṅgala): "Having in some way attained the state of servant of
  Maheśvara… make possible the awakening of the recognition of the Lord" — the whole book
  is the awakening of recognition (the thesis).
- **ĪPK IV, 16, 18** (the "new way," mārgo navaḥ): the Pratyabhijñā is for all beings,
  "no restriction" on who is qualified.
- The Buddhist pūrvapakṣa (ĪPK I.2) is announced — the antagonist to be refuted.

## 4. THESIS LITERATURE-REVIEW VALUE
- **The felt of recognition** (Q1, Q2): the *surprise*/*satisfaction* = the paper's
  camatkāra ↔ Solms' felt-is-primary.
- **Suffering as mis-recognition** (Q3): the paper's "suffering is mis-recognition;
  transformation is re-rendering."
- **The paradox structure**: recognition requires a prior difference-from-self (the same
  yet other) — this is the paper's account of why recognition is *felt* (it crosses a gap).

## 5. IPVV TRANSLATION HOOKS
- **pratyabhijñā** (recognition) — the master term; flag every occurrence.
- **ātman** (Self) — the heart of subjectivity, "ce qui permet à tout sujet de
  s'appréhender comme soi-même."
- **paratva** (alterity) / **bheda** (difference) / **abheda** (non-difference) — the
  identity-problem vocabulary.
- **ānanda/camatkāra** — the felt register (carried by "satisfaction" here; explicit in Ch7).

---
*The intro is the thesis in nuce: recognition is a felt surprise (victory + defeat) that
crosses a self-difference; suffering is misrecognition; the Pratyabhijñā is the awakening
of recognition. Use Q1 as the paper's opening quote.*
